    img.alt = alt;
    caption.innerHTML = cap || '';
    overlay.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'false');
    document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
    closeBtn.focus();
  }

  function close() {
    overlay.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    img.src = '';
    document.body.style.overflow = '';
    if (returnFocus) returnFocus.focus();
  }

  closeBtn.addEventListener('click', close);
  overlay.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    if (e.target === overlay) close();
  });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if (overlay.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'false') return;
    if (e.key === 'Escape') { close(); e.preventDefault(); }

    });
  });
})();

<li><a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a></li>\n    </ul>\n  </nav>\n\n  <main id=\"main\" class=\"main-content\">\n    <!-- HERO -->\n    <section id=\"hero\" class=\"hero\">\n      <h1>Cross-Family Solver Consensus as a Gold-Free Faithfulness Metric for Natural Language to First-Order Logic Translation</h1>\n      <div class=\"author-line\">AI Inventor &middot; 2026</div>\n      <p class=\"tldr\">\n        Can you tell whether a logic formula says what its English sentence says, without ever seeing the right answer?\n        This paper proposes having several independent LLM families translate the same sentence and checking whether the candidate agrees with them using a Z3 solver.\n        In a pre-registered test on 2,686 real candidates, this <strong>cross-family consensus score</strong> outperforms a prompted LLM judge by <strong>+0.099 AUROC</strong> [+0.049, +0.146], matches a frontier judge at 30 times lower cost, and needs no gold formulas, no training data, and no domain knowledge.\n      </p>\n      <div class=\"hero-links\">\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/exec_summary.pdf\">Read the executive summary</a>\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX\">Code repository</a>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"round-links\">\n        Round reports:\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-1/report.pdf\">Round 1</a> &middot;\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-2/report.pdf\">Round 2</a> &middot;\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/report.pdf\">Round 3</a> &middot;\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-4/report.pdf\">Round 4</a> &middot;\n        <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic@fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-5/report.pdf\">Round 5</a>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n\n    <!-- CONTRIBUTIONS -->\n    <section id=\"contributions\">\n      <h2 class=\"section-heading\">Contributions</h2>\n      <div class=\"contributions-grid\">\n        <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n          <h3>A gold-free, training-free faithfulness metric</h3>\n          <p>Cross-family solver consensus outperforms a prompted LLM judge by +0.099 AUROC [+0.049, +0.146] in a pre-registered test on 2,686 candidates across 292 sentences. It requires no gold formulas, no training, and no domain knowledge. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/experiment-6\">Code: Peer agreement vs paid AI judges on held-out logic</a>)</p>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n          <h3>Mechanism analysis: errors scatter, correct translations converge</h3>\n          <p>The self-information ratio of correct-to-error equivalence classes is 4.45:1. Three diverse model families suffice for 97% of full-pool performance. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/evaluation-2\">Code: Why cross-model agreement flags logic errors</a>)</p>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n          <h3>Perturbation sensitivity across 11 error types</h3>\n          <p>Consensus detects errors with within-base AUROC 0.866 overall and is polarity-symmetric, while LLM judges miss downward edits by 0.12&ndash;0.15 AUROC. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/experiment-8\">Code: Rename-proof logic consensus and error-type tests</a>)</p>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"contrib-card\">\n          <h3>Reusable evaluation set</h3>\n          <p>8,507 labelled NL-to-FOL candidates and 5,102 controlled perturbations with panel-adjudicated labels and per-item scores, released with code. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-1/dataset-1\">Code: Held-out logic translation test set, panel-checked</a>)</p>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n\n    <!-- METHOD -->\n    <section id=\"method\">\n      <h2 class=\"section-heading\">Method</h2>\n      <div class=\"prose\">\n        <p>\n          The input is a natural-language sentence and a candidate FOL formula produced by any system. The goal is a score predicting whether the formula faithfully captures the sentence's meaning, without a gold reference, an ontology, or domain knowledge.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          <strong>Peer generation.</strong> Several LLM families (the paper uses 6&ndash;9) independently translate the sentence into FOL at temperature 0. The candidate under evaluation is excluded from its own peer pool.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          <strong>Predicate alignment.</strong> Different families choose different predicate names (one writes <code>Bird(x)</code>, another <code>is_bird(x)</code>). Before comparison, an aligner maps the candidate's predicates onto each peer's by normalized edit distance, subject to arity consistency and injectivity.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          <strong>Pairwise solver verification.</strong> For each peer, a Z3 satisfiability solver tests whether the aligned candidate and the peer are logically equivalent. A pair is equivalent if Z3 proves both directions of implication unsatisfiable.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          <strong>Consensus score.</strong> The score is <em>1 minus the fraction of peers that are solver-equivalent to the candidate</em>. A high score means most peers disagree, predicting an error. A low score means most peers converge on the same logical content as the candidate.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          <strong>Complementary text checks.</strong> Because consensus is blind to errors that all peers reproduce, two text-based layers (content accounting and a role questionnaire checked against Z3 models of the formula) are combined with the consensus score through a frozen logistic model (PEER+TEXT). (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-1/experiment-1\">Code: Screening a three-layer logic-translation checker</a>; <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-1/experiment-3\">Code: Do other models' translations agree?</a>)\n        </p>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n\n    <!-- RESULTS -->\n    <section id=\"results\">\n      <h2 class=\"section-heading\">Results</h2>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Pre-registered held-out test</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">+0.099 AUROC</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          Cross-family consensus (stratified AUROC 0.741) outperforms the Flash-Lite disguised LLM judge (0.642) by +0.099 [+0.049, +0.146] on Dataset E (2,686 candidates, 292 sentences). The 95% CI excludes zero, confirming the pre-registered hypothesis. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/experiment-6\">Code</a>)\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Templated long-rule sentences</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">0.954 within-template AUROC</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          On 1,904 candidates for 221 templated long-rule sentences with shared predicate vocabulary, consensus achieves 0.954 vs. the judge's 0.587, a delta of +0.367 [+0.328, +0.404]. Error endorsement is exactly zero in this condition. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/experiment-7\">Code</a>)\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Signal beyond all baselines</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">+0.039 nested gain</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          Adding consensus to the full 28-feature baseline stack (S4) yields a stratified AUROC gain of +0.039 [+0.021, +0.057], with a permutation-null 95th percentile of 0.009. Consensus carries information orthogonal to judges, round-trip, and self-consistency.\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Frontier-judge parity at 30x lower cost</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">0.957 ratio</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          On a 284-row subsample, the ratio of consensus AUROC to the frontier judge (Gemini 3.1 Pro) is 0.957 [0.887, 1.034]. Consensus costs ~$1.2 &times; 10<sup>-4</sup> per candidate vs. $3.7 &times; 10<sup>-3</sup> for the frontier judge.\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Three families suffice</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">97% of full-pool AUROC at k = 3</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          The AUROC curve saturates at 3 families (0.757 vs. 0.784 at k = 7). Leave-one-family-out analysis shows no single family drives the signal.\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <div class=\"result-row\">\n        <div class=\"result-label\">Perturbation suite</div>\n        <div class=\"result-number\">0.866 overall within-base AUROC</div>\n        <div class=\"result-context\">\n          Across 4,234 typed mutants and 868 controls spanning 11 error types, consensus achieves within-base AUROC 0.84&ndash;0.88 per operator. It is polarity-symmetric (DOWN/UP difference &lt; 0.01), while LLM judges miss downward edits by 0.12&ndash;0.15 AUROC. (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-eff060-layered-gold-free-checks-for-logic/tree/fork/run_qck1d05BqxkX/round-3/experiment-8\">Code</a>)\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <h3 style=\"font-size:17px; font-weight:600; margin:32px 0 12px;\">Main comparison table (Dataset E)</h3>\n      <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n        <table class=\"data-table\">\n          <thead>\n            <tr>\n              <th>Metric</th>\n              <th>Pooled AUROC [95% CI]</th>\n              <th>Strat. AUROC [95% CI]</th>\n              <th>$/item</th>\n            </tr>\n          </thead>\n          <tbody>\n            <tr><td>S4 + consensus</td><td>0.807 [0.772, 0.838]</td><td>0.774 [0.743, 0.802]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>PEER+TEXT (fused)</td><td>0.790 [0.752, 0.825]</td><td>0.753 [0.720, 0.784]</td><td>1.2&times;10<sup>-4</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Cross-family consensus</td><td>0.782 [0.745, 0.816]</td><td>0.741 [0.705, 0.775]</td><td>1.2&times;10<sup>-4</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Stacked baselines (S4)</td><td>0.777 [0.739, 0.809]</td><td>0.735 [0.699, 0.766]</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Local Qwen3-8B judge (disg.)</td><td>0.710 [0.674, 0.746]</td><td>0.674 [0.646, 0.703]</td><td>0</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>GPT-4.1-Nano judge (orig.)</td><td>0.700 [0.659, 0.739]</td><td>0.653 [0.616, 0.688]</td><td>2.0&times;10<sup>-5</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Flash-Lite judge (disg.)</td><td>0.696 [0.655, 0.733]</td><td>0.642 [0.607, 0.676]</td><td>4.9&times;10<sup>-5</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Self-consistency (SC-5)</td><td>0.656 [0.609, 0.699]</td><td>0.598 [0.559, 0.637]</td><td>2.9&times;10<sup>-5</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Round-trip NLI</td><td>0.639 [0.593, 0.687]</td><td>0.606 [0.569, 0.645]</td><td>2.7&times;10<sup>-5</sup></td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Flash-Lite judge (orig.)</td><td>0.635 [0.595, 0.671]</td><td>0.623 [0.593, 0.651]</td><td>4.9&times;10<sup>-5</sup></td></tr>\n          </tbody>\n        </table>\n      </div>\n\n      <h3 style=\"font-size:17px; font-weight:600; margin:32px 0 12px;\">Perturbation sensitivity (within-base AUROC, selected operators)</h3>\n      <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n        <table class=\"data-table\">\n          <thead>\n            <tr><th>Metric</th><th>Overall</th><th>NEG</th><th>QUANT</th><th>CONN</th><th>DROP</th><th>ADD</th><th>SWAP</th></tr>\n          </thead>\n          <tbody>\n            <tr><td>Consensus (align)</td><td>0.866</td><td>0.87</td><td>0.86</td><td>0.86</td><td>0.84</td><td>0.86</td><td>0.88</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Flash-Lite judge (disg.)</td><td>0.680</td><td>0.70</td><td>0.62</td><td>0.65</td><td>0.58</td><td>0.69</td><td>0.53</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>SC-5</td><td>0.666</td><td>0.67</td><td>0.65</td><td>0.65</td><td>0.65</td><td>0.65</td><td>0.63</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>L2-bow</td><td>0.659</td><td>0.50</td><td>0.50</td><td>0.50</td><td>0.97</td><td>0.85</td><td>0.50</td></tr>\n            <tr><td>Structural metrics</td><td>~0.50</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td></tr>\n          </tbody>\n        </table>\n      </div>\n    </section>\n\n    <!-- FIGURES -->\n    <section id=\"figures\">\n      <h2 class=\"section-heading\">Figures</h2>\n      <div class=\"gallery\">\n        <div class=\"gallery-item\">\n          <button type=\"button\" aria-label=\"Enlarge: Consensus vs. judges on held-out data\" data-lightbox=\"figures/fig2_v0.png\" data-caption=\"Stratified AUROC for detecting NL-to-FOL translation errors on Dataset E (R_AB labels, n = 2,686 candidates, 292 sentences). Blue bars are consensus-based metrics and grey bars are baselines and LLM judges. Cross-family consensus (0.741) scores above every LLM judge (0.623&ndash;0.674), round-trip NLI (0.606) and self-consistency (0.598). The bracket marks the pre-registered delta, +0.099 [+0.049, +0.146].\">\n            <img src=\"figures/fig2_v0.png\" alt=\"Horizontal bar chart comparing stratified AUROC of consensus-based metrics (blue) against LLM judges and baselines (grey) on Dataset E. S4 + consensus leads at 0.774, cross-family consensus is 0.741, and Flash-Lite judge is 0.642. A bracket shows the pre-registered delta of +0.099.\" loading=\"lazy\">\n          </button>\n          <p class=\"gallery-caption\">\n            <strong>Consensus vs. judges on held-out data.</strong> Stratified AUROC for detecting NL-to-FOL translation errors on Dataset E (R<sub>AB</sub> labels, n = 2,686 candidates, 292 sentences). Cross-family consensus (0.741) scores above every LLM judge (0.623&ndash;0.674), round-trip NLI (0.606) and self-consistency (0.598). Public web page and paper source for the research on cross-family solver consensus as a gold-free faithfulness metric for natural language to first-order logic translation.

- `index.html` — self-contained public web page (GitHub Pages site)
- `paper.tex` — LaTeX source of the paper
- `paper.pdf` — compiled paper
- `references.bib` — bibliography
- `figures/` — all figures used by the paper and the web page
  - `fig2_v0.pdf` / `fig2_v0.png` — main comparison chart (consensus vs judges on Dataset E)
  - `fig3_v0.pdf` / `fig3_v0.png` — consensus advantage by sentence complexity
  - `fig4_v0.pdf` / `fig4_v0.png` — error scatter vs correct convergence histogram
- `workspace/` — scratch folder from the LaTeX build (can be ignored)

## How to view

Open `index.html` in any browser. It is fully self-contained with no external dependencies.
